newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy car mkt strong but signs demand falling-CSP.
newsitem.headline: Italy car mkt strong but signs demand falling-CSP.

text.p: Italy's car buying incentive program is continuing to boost the domestic auto market but for the first time in several months dealers are beginning to see signs of slackening demand, car sector research body CSP said.
CSP said in a statement that in June half the new cars sold benefited from the bonus scheme for scrapping old cars for new vehicles which the government introduced in January.

Transport Ministry data published on Wednesday showed that Italian new car registrations jumped 50 percent in June to 222,800 over June last year. The figures for the first half were also good, showing a 31 percent rise to 1.31 million.
CSP said it forecast the Italian car market closing 1997 with 2.25 million new registrations, up 30 percent from 1996.

But it noted that in its regular monthly survey of car dealers, 30 percent of those polled described the volume of new orders as low, with only 28 percent seeing it as high, against 87 percent giving a positive judgment in February.
For the coming months, negative forecasts for demand outnumbered positive expectations by 22 percent against 21 percent, while 57 percent saw an unchanged trend.
